newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian 96/97 exporter cocoa rates agreed.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian 96/97 exporter cocoa rates agreed.

text.p: Ivory Coast set reference rates to be paid to cocoa buyers and exporters on Monday, clearing the way for its belated 1996/97 marketing season to get fully underway, a trade source said.
The government took the decision at a cabinet meeting but details were not immediately available, the source said, adding that exporters' demands had not been fully met.
"Buyers commissions are about the same but the rates are not very interesting for exporters," the source said after receiving details.
"Exporters are obliged to meet their existing contracts but after that they will have to look at where they stand," the source added.

Exporters had been demanding an increase in their guideline rate for 1996/97 to cope with cost inflation in 1995/96, re-equiping for loading bulk as well as bagged cocoa, and costs under a government proposal for them to collect buyers' income taxes.

Ivory Coast opened its 1996/97 cocoa marketing season on October 24, setting an unchanged reference farmgate price of 320 CFA francs per bagged kg and an export tax down 10 CFA to 140 CFA per kg. Usually the season starts in early October.
